title: cuda: add capture/replay support with shape guards and warmup to mitigate regressions
author: Liam Chen
description:
Introduce optional CUDA graph capture/replay for commonly-seen kernel sequences in the inference runtime. Motivation: reduce CPU scheduling overhead and kernel launch latency for stable request shapes/lengths. This PR implements a lightweight capture manager, runtime shape guards that validate compatibility to replay captured graphs, an LRU eviction + time-based expiry for captured graphs, and a warmup heuristic to pre-populate likely graphs to avoid cold-start regressions. The description below covers motivation, design, tests, and known tradeoffs.

Motivation: in production we observed CPU-side overhead from per-request kernel launches and CUDA stream synchronization in high-throughput routes. CUDA graphs can collapse recurring sequences into a single replay step and reduce overhead, but naive capture causes correctness/regression issues when tensor shapes/strides vary or when the first captured execution is slow (warmup spike).

Design:
- GraphManager: tracks capture keys derived from (model id, kernel sequence signature, shapes, dtypes, strides) and stores cuGraph/cuGraphExec handles.
- Shape guards: each captured graph has a compact shape guard (shape tuple + strides + static dims mask). Replays only when guard matches; otherwise fallback to regular execution path.
- Warmup: configurable warmup_count (default 2) triggers synthetic warmup runs for a newly created capture key using representative input (taken from recent requests or a supplied warmup prompt). Warmup runs are run as non-blocking async tasks and gated by a per-model rate limiter.
- Eviction/policy: LRU with max_graphs per-device and ttl_seconds-for-unused to avoid unbounded memory and stale captures from model rollouts.
- Metrics and tracing: per-graph replay rate, fallback reasons (shape-mismatch, capacity-evicted), warmup_success and warmup_latency.
- Config: runtime.cuda_graphs.enabled (bool), runtime.cuda_graphs.warmup_count (int), runtime.cuda_graphs.max_graphs (int), runtime.cuda_graphs.shape_guard_mode ("strict"|"relaxed").

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for GraphManager lifecycle, guard matching, and eviction.
- E2E perf job that measures p50/p95/p99 for representative workloads (chat streaming, long completion).
- Stress test to exercise frequent shape variation and confirm fallback correctness.

Performance summary (internal):
- Stable sequence workloads: p99 latency reduced by 8-15% and CPU utilization dropped by ~20% in our perf lab.
- Mixed-shape workloads: throughput unchanged but initial-first-request latency improved after warmup; without warmup we observed up to 30% first-request regression.

Migration strategy: feature gated behind runtime.cuda_graphs.enabled=false by default. Docs include instructions and recommended defaults for production.

Rollout plan: gradual canary on dedicated pools, enable on model-level opt-ins, monitor metrics (replay_rate, fallback_rate, warmup_failures).

Known limitations:
- Some models with highly dynamic per-token tensor shapes (e.g., variable kv-cache layout due to custom batching) may rarely benefit.
- Warmup adds a small background cost; ephemeral models (single-run) may not benefit.
- Strict shape guards can reduce capture hit-rate; relaxed mode will permit some compatible stride/size differences at the cost of more careful correctness checks.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement GraphManager and capture/replay paths
- [x] Add shape guard and fallback logic
- [x] Add warmup heuristic and config flags
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] E2E perf benchmark updates
- [x] Docs and release notes

release_notes: Adds optional CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards and warmup to reduce kernel launch overhead. Feature is disabled by default; enable via runtime.cuda_graphs.enabled. Improves p99 in stable workloads and provides fallbacks to avoid correctness regressions.
discussion_summary: Discussion focused on correctness (shape/stride compatibility) and avoiding regressions seen in prior attempts to enable CUDA graphs.
Consensus: gate feature behind config, introduce warmup to avoid first-request spikes, provide conservative default guards and a relaxed mode for throughput-oriented workloads.
Operational guidance: enable on canaries first, monitor replay_rate/fallback_rate/warmup_failures metrics.
performance_results: Stable sequence workload (chat-long): p50 same, p95 -6%, p99 -12% in lab runs
CPU user time: ~20% reduction on high throughput routes in perf lab
Mixed-shape workload: throughput ~0% change, warmup avoids initial 20-30% first-request latency regression
Memory: graph cache used ~400MB/device for default max_graphs=64 in benchmark model
